html:
SMTO-ART-0022 — The Gateway can't give this Task its own temporary folder

GUID: be3f065b-6a31-4602-bfcb-f6e38aa17932
Slug: tmp-mapping-unavailable
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • On Linux, the Gateway (the helper program that runs commands on a computer) gives each Task a private /tmp folder. That computer can't set this up, so a file action using it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to run the Gateway installer again, or to install the 'bubblewrap' package on it. The Gateway uses bubblewrap to create the private /tmp folder, and the Linux installer includes it.
  2. After that, send the request again in a new message. SMTO checks the Gateway's temporary-folder support when a Task starts, so a new Task picks up the fix.

What success looks like

  • In the new Task, the file action finishes without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't ask SMTO to use the computer's shared /tmp folder instead; other programs keep their files there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway could not build the run's /tmp bind mount: the host is not Linux, bubblewrap (bwrap) is not on PATH, the original user namespace could not be verified, or a mapped Files operation had no run temp directory.

What this means

  • Temporary mapping requests a non-Linux platform, cannot find bubblewrap or encounters an OS error constructing the mount invocation. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Temporary mapping requests a non-Linux platform, cannot find bubblewrap or encounters an OS error constructing the mount invocation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect platform, bubblewrap availability and the actual mount helper failure.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, confirm the platform is Linux, that bwrap is installed and on PATH (src/gateway_agent/install.sh installs bubblewrap; the installation check lists bwrap), and that /proc/self/ns/user is readable. Then start a new run so artifact_tmp_mapping is negotiated again; shell launches already fall back to managed TMPDIR, but Files find and path operations on a mapped run fail with this error.
  • Use the supported Gateway mapping flow and resolve the named platform/helper failure without bypassing scope checks.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported mapping or the existing explicit fallback policy handles the intended execution envelope.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
